name: Burpee

technique.setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart and clear floor space in front of you. Pick a pace you can keep for the whole interval.
cues: Squat down and plant the hands under the shoulders
Jump or step the feet back to a straight plank
Bring the feet back under the hips and stand tall
Land softly on the balls of the feet with knees bent
mistakes: Letting the hips sag in the plank and arching the lower back
Landing stiff-legged from the jump
Rushing so form breaks down halfway through the interval
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist or knee
Dizziness or chest pain
Lower back pain when the feet kick back

media.searchHint: Bodyweight Warrior how to do a burpee beginner modification

notes: Scaled version: step the feet back and forward one at a time, skip the push-up and replace the jump with a rise onto the toes; add the jump back first, then the step-free kick-back.

name: Mountain climber

technique.setup: Start in a high plank with hands under the shoulders and the body in a straight line from head to heels.
cues: Push the floor away and keep the shoulders over the hands
Drive one knee toward the chest, then switch
Keep the hips level with the shoulders
Breathe steadily and keep the pace even
mistakes: Piking the hips up high
Shoulders drifting behind the hands
Bouncing the hips side to side
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
Lower back pain

notes: Slow version: step each knee in with a 1 s pause, which also works as core work.

name: Kettlebell swing

technique.setup: Stand with feet a little wider than the hips and the kettlebell about a foot in front of you. Hinge at the hips with a flat back and grip the handle with both hands.
cues: Hinge at the hips, it is not a squat
Hike the bell back high between the thighs
Snap the hips forward and squeeze the glutes to float the bell to chest height
Keep the lower back neutral and ribs down at the top
mistakes: Squatting the bell down instead of hinging
Lifting the bell with the arms
Rounding the lower back at the bottom
Leaning back at the top
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the lower back
Numbness or tingling down the leg
Losing grip or control of the bell

media.searchHint: two hand kettlebell swing hip hinge tutorial beginner

notes: Learn the hinge with kettlebell-rdl first. Start light (8-12 kg); to stop, let the bell swing back and park it on the floor in front of you.

name: Box jump

technique.setup: Stand about a foot from a stable box that will not slide, starting low (30-40 cm). After every rep step down one foot at a time, never jump down.
cues: Swing the arms back and dip the hips
Jump up and land softly with the whole foot on the box
Knees track over the toes on landing
Stand tall, then step down one foot at a time
mistakes: Jumping back down off the box
Knees caving in on landing
Picking a box so high you land in a deep squat
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the knee
Ankle or Achilles pain
Clipping the box edge with the toes

notes: Raise box height only when every landing is quiet and stable.

name: Slam ball

technique.setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a non-bouncing slam ball at the chest. Use a light ball (4-6 kg) to start.
cues: Reach the ball overhead with ribs down
Slam it down hard in front of the feet
Hinge at the hips with a flat back to pick it up
Brace the core before every slam
mistakes: Rounding the lower back to pick the ball up
Arching the back hard at the top
Using a bouncy ball that rebounds into the face
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the lower back or shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder overhead

notes: Needs a slam ball, which the equipment list cannot express (logged here as floor).

name: Bear crawl

technique.setup: Start on hands and knees with hands under the shoulders and knees under the hips, then lift the knees a few centimetres off the floor.
cues: Keep the knees hovering just off the floor
Move the opposite hand and foot together
Keep the back flat and hips low
Take small steps and push the floor away
mistakes: Hips shooting up high
Moving the same-side hand and foot together
Taking big steps that twist the hips
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist
Pinching at the front of the shoulder

notes: Crawl forward and backward over a few metres, or hold the hover in place if space is short.

name: Jumping jack

technique.setup: Stand tall with feet together and arms by your sides.
cues: Jump the feet out wide as the arms sweep overhead
Jump back to feet together, arms down
Stay light on the balls of the feet
Keep a soft bend in the knees
mistakes: Landing flat-footed and heavy
Locking the knees on landing
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the knee or ankle
Dizziness or chest pain

media.searchHint: how to do jumping jacks correctly low impact step jack

notes: Low-impact version: step one foot out at a time instead of jumping.

name: High knees

technique.setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and arms bent at 90 degrees.
cues: Drive each knee up to hip height
Land softly on the balls of the feet
Stand tall and pump the arms
Keep a quick, steady rhythm
mistakes: Leaning back as the knees come up
Knees only reaching halfway
Stomping the feet down
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the knee, hip or ankle
Dizziness or chest pain

media.searchHint: high knees exercise proper form tutorial

notes: Marching high knees (no hop) is the low-impact version.

name: Shuttle run

technique.setup: Mark two lines 5-10 m apart on a non-slip surface. Run between them for the interval, touching the line at each turn.
cues: Lower the hips and shorten the steps before each turn
Plant the outside foot and push off in the new direction
Touch the line with the hand closest to it
Accelerate out of every turn
mistakes: Turning upright with straight legs
Knees caving in on the turn
Sliding into the line on a slippery floor
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the knee or ankle
A twist or give-way feeling in the knee

media.searchHint: shuttle run turn technique conditioning drill

notes: Needs 5-10 m of clear space; the equipment list has no value for space, so it is logged as none.

name: Skipping

technique.setup: Hold the rope handles at hip height with elbows close to the sides. Without a rope, mimic the same movement.
cues: Turn the rope with the wrists, not the arms
Make small, quick hops on the balls of the feet
Keep the knees soft and the body tall
mistakes: Jumping too high
Landing flat-footed
Swinging the rope with the whole arm
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the ankle or knee
Calf or Achilles pain

notes: Needs a skipping rope, which the equipment list cannot express (logged as none; rope-less skipping works too).
